name: APEX Accelerators (formerly Procurement Technical Assistance Centers)
what: [APEX Accelerators](#term:apex-accelerator) (formerly known as Procurement Technical Assistance Centers) provide technical assistance to businesses interested in selling products or services to federal, state, and local governments [260](#cite:260). The program is administered by the DoD [Office of Small Business Programs](#term:osdbu) through [cooperative agreements](#term:grant) with state and local governments and non-profits [258](#cite:258). As of October 2023 the network had 90-plus APEX Accelerators with over 300 local offices and more than 600 procurement advisers [258](#cite:258). Ohio's host page lists bid preparation help, bid-matching, military specifications, one-on-one training and procurement histories, at no charge to Ohio businesses [259](#cite:259).
who_for: Businesses interested in selling products or services to federal, state and local governments [260](#cite:260)
how_to_find: SBA points to the national locator at https://www.apexaccelerators.us/#/ [260](#cite:260). State hosts may run their own finders; Ohio's county finder is at https://find.govcontracts.ohio.gov/contact/ [259](#cite:259).

conflicts: Left out of the description until a government source is read: network size (nearly 1,000 local centers, hosted by universities, colleges, state economic development agencies and private partners), which comes only from the network's own association while SBA's page gives no count [263](#cite:263) [262](#cite:262)

what: [Small Business Development Centers](#term:sbdc) give individual advising and technical assistance on capital, planning, technology, marketing and export [262](#cite:262). what: MBDA Business Centers belong to the Commerce Department's Minority Business Development Agency, whose site was live on 2026-10-03 and describes Business Centers in general terms, with no count, locator or status notice in the fetched text [267](#cite:267). Executive Order 14238 of March 14, 2025 called for eliminating MBDA, and on May 13, 2025 the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island issued a preliminary injunction in State of Rhode Island et al. v. Trump et al. [270](#cite:270). A state-hosted centre in North Carolina still presents itself as operating and as one of 35 such centers [268](#cite:268). Before 2025, [CRS](#term:crs) counted 131 Business Centers as of FY2023 including specialty centers, with 40 standard Business Centers in 32 states and Puerto Rico [269](#cite:269).

name: FAST partners (state SBIR/STTR support organisations)
what: A [FAST partner](#term:fast-program) is an organization funded under [SBA](#term:sba)'s FAST Partnership Program to help firms in its state or region compete for [SBIR](#term:sbir)/[STTR](#term:sttr) [128](#cite:128). FAST's three functions are stakeholder engagement, [technical and business assistance](#term:taba), and financial support such as Phase 0 and travel [grants](#term:grant) [252](#cite:252). SBA announced 50 [FY 2026](#term:fiscal-year) awardee organizations on September 22, 2026, covering 49 states and Puerto Rico; examples are University of Illinois, Arizona Commerce Authority, Ben Franklin Technology Partners (Pennsylvania), Puerto Rico Science, Technology & Research Trust and Central Washington University [130](#cite:130).
who_for: Small firms preparing SBIR/STTR proposals; SBA frames the aim as more proposals and awards "from small businesses owners in undercapitalized regions." [128](#cite:128)
how_to_find: The state-by-state table in SBA's September 22, 2026 announcement [130](#cite:130). Current awardees are also listed on SBA's FAST page, with contact FAST@sba.gov [128](#cite:128). SBA's Lab to Market Hub is a resource finder by industry, organization type, location and award status that links FAST [131](#cite:131).

name: State SBIR/STTR match and Phase 0 programs (examples)
what: [SBA](#term:sba)'s September 2020 table lists 25 states with [Phase I](#term:phase-i)/II matching programs and 20 states and territories with [Phase 0](#term:fast-program) [grants](#term:grant); it is six years old and serves only as a pointer list [253](#cite:253). North Carolina's One North Carolina Small Business Program made 32 matching awards totaling $2,368,507 in FY2026 and also runs an incentive solicitation [254]. Kentucky matches up to $100,000 for Phase I and up to $150,000 for Phase II, for firms "based in, or willing to re-locate to, Kentucky" [255]. Alabama's Supplemental Grant Program offers up to $100,000 for Phase I and up to $250,000 for Phase II (50% of the award), and applications were closed when the page was read [256]. Massachusetts START grants of $100,000 to $500,000 go to Massachusetts companies with an [SBIR](#term:sbir)/[STTR](#term:sttr) [Phase II](#term:phase-ii) in the past 5 years; the 2026 round opened February 1 and closed February 23, 2026 [257](#cite:257).
who_for: For-profit SBIR or STTR recipients in a state that runs such a program, as in Kentucky's rule [255](#cite:255)
how_to_find: North Carolina: https://www.commerce.nc.gov/grants-incentives/technology-funds/one-north-carolina-small-business-program [254](#cite:254). Kentucky: https://newkentuckyhome.ky.gov/Entrepreneurship/SBIR_STTR [255](#cite:255). Alabama: https://innovatealabama.org/programs/supplemental-grant-program/ [256](#cite:256). Massachusetts: https://www.mass.gov/news/massventures-opens-start-grant-applications-to-help-startups-translate-research-into-companies-and-jobs [257](#cite:257). FAST partners may also offer "Phase 0" proposal-development grants or loans [128](#cite:128).
